text:
Marathon's stock edged up 0.28% today, holding near $475 after a volatile two weeks that saw it gain nearly 10% overall. The modest move reflects conflicting signals: crude oil prices fell today as traders bet on diplomatic progress in the Middle East, which typically pressures refiner margins, but the broader geopolitical backdrop—Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities, Iranian warnings, and shipping strikes in the Strait of Hormuz—keeps crude prices elevated enough to stay above $100 per barrel. Refineries are running at 93.5% capacity, near full utilization, which limits upside from higher oil prices but also means the company can't easily adjust throughput if margins tighten.

The stock's 10% rally over two weeks sits on top of an oil market caught between fear and hope: Brent crude topped $109 earlier in the week after reported attacks on Saudi Arabia, but today's move down on diplomatic optimism shows traders are hedging geopolitical risk rather than fully pricing it in. That uncertainty is typical for refiners during Middle East tension—they benefit from elevated crude prices but face a ceiling if markets start to believe the risk will resolve.
